tasks.title: SCS-001 Insight Agent — prompt.md (identity + constitutional mandate)

strengths: Constitutional mandate is prominently placed and operationalised with a concrete rubric threshold (≥90% gate) and explicit failure examples — this directly satisfies the 'why does this matter' requirement from the spec.
Accuracy obligation explicitly prohibits quote fabrication and grounds the agent to metadata-only sources, which is critical for Block B mode where no real video is available.
Hook Formula Library is well-designed: each formula is tied to a measurable score factor, making selection deterministic rather than arbitrary.
Character limits on all commentary and hook fields are clearly stated and match the locked contract constraints.
Budget constraint is restated in the prompt, giving the agent awareness of the $2/day ceiling even though enforcement is external.
Block B mode caveat is explicit and correctly scoped — prevents the agent from hallucinating video content it cannot access.
Constitutional mandate is explicit and testable ('≥90% of outputs must pass rubric')
Accuracy obligation clearly prohibits fabrication — protects against hallucination
Hook Formula Library provides concrete patterns with examples, reducing ambiguity
Output contract is fully specified with field limits and enum constraints
Budget constraint is stated ($2/day) and traceable to ClawRouter cost model
Block B mode clarifies that metadata-only derivation is the constraint, not a limitation
Pre-clip and post-clip commentary fields enable editorial control without agent overreach
why_does_this_matter field is properly bounded (20-500 chars) to prevent both truncation and verbosity

tasks.title: SCS-001 Insight Agent — index.ts (core agent logic + Claude Sonnet integration)

issues.description: File is truncated mid-string literal inside buildPrompt(). The string 'pre_clip_commentary' is cut off with no closing quote, no closing bracket for the array, no return statement, and no closing brace for the function. The file is syntactically invalid TypeScript and will not compile.

All core agent logic is missing: the Claude Sonnet API call via ClawRouter, the JSON extraction using indexOf/lastIndexOf (as specified), the InsightBrief assembly function, the main runInsightAgent() or equivalent entry point, and any export of the primary agent function. The file delivers only type definitions and mock data — zero runnable agent logic.
Spec requires JSON extraction using indexOf/lastIndexOf (no regex). This is entirely absent — the implementation was never reached before truncation.
CLAWROUTER_URL is referenced but the HTTP fetch/call to ClawRouter is never implemented. The constant is declared but dead code in the current state.
No validation that input clips have qualified === true before processing, which is a stated contract requirement ('qualified === true only').
cloud_cost_usd field is declared in the InsightBrief interface but there is no logic to compute or populate it — no token counting or cost estimation is present.

File ends mid-function at line ~45. The buildPrompt() return statement is incomplete (cuts off at 'pre_clip_commentary'). Missing: rest of prompt template, generateInsight() function, ClawRouter HTTP call, JSON extraction logic (indexOf/lastIndexOf), error handling, and exports.
No insight generation logic present. Task requires: call ClawRouter at CLAWROUTER_URL, extract JSON response using indexOf/lastIndexOf, map to InsightBrief contract. None of this is implemented.
buildPrompt() does not complete. The prompt template is cut off mid-key. The function must return a complete, valid prompt string ready for Claude Sonnet.
No contract validation. InsightBrief interface is defined but no code validates output against contracts/scs-001/insight-brief-v1.json or ensures all required fields are populated.

tasks.title: SCS-001 Insight Agent — validate-insight-output.ts (Block B integration test)

strengths: No fence contamination — file is clean TypeScript.
Correctly implements the full validation pipeline: getMockQualifiedClips() → InsightAgent.run() → InsightBrief[] checks.
All spec-required field validations are present: hook.text ≤80 chars, hook.formula enum check, pre/post_clip_commentary ≤200 chars, why_does_this_matter substantive check, clip_id back-link.
Block B gate (≥90% why_does_this_matter pass rate) is correctly computed and asserted.
Process exit code handling is correct — uses process.exitCode accumulation pattern rather than early exit, so all checks run and all failures are reported.
Cloud cost aggregation and reporting is a useful operational addition.
Shebang line and async main() pattern are appropriate for ts-node execution.
Error boundary on main() with process.exit(1) prevents silent failures.
No fence contamination — file is valid executable TypeScript
Spec compliance: all required checks present (hook.text ≤80, hook.formula enum, pre/post_clip_commentary ≤200, why_does_this_matter substantive, clip_id back-links)
Block B gate correctly implemented: tracks whyPassCount and enforces ≥90% threshold
Proper async/await for agent.run()
Clear assertion function with pass/fail logging
Validates input mock clips (qualified === true, quality_score >= 20)
Tracks clipIds set for back-link validation
Comprehensive field validation (insight_id prefix, speaker_name, cloud_cost_usd, hook_formula_used)
Outputs total cloud cost and clear pass/fail summary
Proper exit codes (0 = pass, 1 = fail)
No hardcoded values that should be configurable — VALID_FORMULAS and GENERIC_PHRASES are constants at top
